rounds.proof_sketch: For shape [16,256,256] with dim=0: grid_size_original=256, grid_size_mutant=255. Missing block 255 has batch_idx=255. Guard 'if (batch_idx >= batch) return;' with batch=16 means block 255 would return immediately. The removed block contributes zero useful work.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation removes block 255 from the 1D grid launch for the dim=0 case. However, the kernel has an early-exit guard 'if (batch_idx >= batch) return;' that fires when batch_idx >= 16. Since block 255 would have batch_idx=255, which is far greater than 16, this block would immediately return without performing any computation. Both the original and mutated versions execute exactly the same useful work: only blocks 0-15 process the reduction. No value-level input can change this because the guard is independent of tensor values.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract because the removed block's work is structurally unreachable due to the guard predicate. Killing would require changing batch dimension to >255, which violates the fixed-shape constraint.
rounds.recommendations: When testing launch configuration mutations, verify whether the affected blocks/threads actually contribute to the output by tracing guard conditions. Guard predicates can render blocks unreachable even when launched, making certain launch config changes semantically equivalent.
